checked_claims.claim: The authors compare the geometric distance of an anchor to a fit that omits that geometric constraint but retains its Cepheids and calibrates with the other two anchors.
checked_claims.limit: This is the paper physical variant. It does not establish that deleting one row from the frozen released compact product reproduces that variant.

evidence.locator: §4.7 printed p25; Figure19 left panel printed p40

checked_claims.claim: The displayed y vector subtracts the adopted NGC4258 geometric modulus from retained NGC4258 Cepheid apparent Wesenheit magnitudes; the fit adds a distance-offset parameter.
checked_claims.limit: Subtracting a known reference can be a coordinate translation, but an independently meaningful holdout needs a consistently transformed prior and an explicit source/reduction contract. The full-fit source box cannot be claimed free of heldout information.

checked_claims.claim: The released prior box is centered on the supplied least-squares best-fit coordinates, with half-width equal to supplied standard widths times PRIOR_WIDTH_RATIO=10. Source log_prior returns a constant 1 inside the closed box and -infinity outside.
checked_claims.limit: No training-only or independently specified prior is provided by these checked sources. Source prose calls this essentially prior-free; it is a finite data-derived box, not evidence of heldout independence.

checked_claims.claim: Artificial-star background calibration uses the expected Cepheid magnitude from its period and trial P–L fits, iteratively updates photometry, and assigns a within-host covariance floor based on 20% of the background correction.
checked_claims.limit: The source says this particular background component has no inter-host covariance because each host trial relation is calibrated independently. This does not establish zero covariance for the full data vector, anchor calibrations, metallicity, or SN data.
